items.answer: information regarding the readability of the transmission.

items.prompt: Operating at a non-controlled aerodrome — fill the blank: ‘ I n the vicinity’ is within _____ and at a height above the aerodrome that could result in conflict with operations at the aerodrome.

items.prompt: Operating at a non-controlled aerodrome — Before arriving at a non-controlled aerodrome, pilots should monitor their radios and broadcast their intentions in accordance with the following (a)?
items.answer: When in the vicinity of an aerodrome published on aeronautical charts, listen and broadcast as necessary on the CTAF (126.7 MHz if not nominated or discrete).

items.prompt: Operating at a non-controlled aerodrome — Before arriving at a non-controlled aerodrome, pilots should monitor their radios and broadcast their intentions in accordance with the following (b)?
items.answer: When aerodromes are located within a Mandatory Broadcast Area, listen and broadcast as necessary on the frequency for the Mandatory Broadcast Area.

items.prompt: Operating at a non-controlled aerodrome — Before arriving at a non-controlled aerodrome, pilots should monitor their radios and broadcast their intentions in accordance with the following (c)?
items.answer: In all other cases, CASA recommends that pilots listen and broadcast as necessary on the Area Frequency.

items.prompt: Operating at a non-controlled aerodrome — fill the blank: • An AFRU confirmation will be either the name of the aerodrome plus ‘ CTAF ’ or, if any aircraft transmissions have been received by the AFRU within the last _____ , a low volume 300 millisecond tone.
items.answer: 5 minutes
distractors: 10 minutes
1 minute
45 minutes

items.prompt: Parachute operations in non-controlled — fill the blank: If the parachuting occurs in the vicinity of a non-controlled aerodrome, an additional broadcast should be made not less than _____ before the parachutists leave the aircraft.
items.answer: 4 minutes

15 minutes
10 minutes

items.prompt: Non-controlled aerodromes with an aerodrome — Communications at aerodromes with local flight information services are like those at other non- controlled aerodromes without these services, except that (a)?
items.answer: during hours of operation of the aerodrome information service, a pilot should initiate communication by calling the service ‘ (unit identifier) INFORMATION/RADIO ’ (as appropriate to the service provided - AFIS, SFIS or CA/GRS)

items.prompt: Non-controlled aerodromes with an aerodrome — Communications at aerodromes with local flight information services are like those at other non- controlled aerodromes without these services, except that (b)?
items.answer: after the initial communication according to subparagraph a., subsequent reports should be addressed to ‘ (location) TRAFFIC'

items.prompt: Non-controlled aerodromes with an aerodrome — Communications at aerodromes with local flight information services are like those at other non- controlled aerodromes without these services, except that (c)?
items.answer: positional reports specified for the 10NM position should instead be made at or before the boundary of the relevant Broadcast Area (BA)

items.prompt: Non-controlled aerodromes with an aerodrome — Communications at aerodromes with local flight information services are like those at other non- controlled aerodromes without these services, except that (d)?
items.answer: the service at some locations requires a departure report for both IFR and VFR aircraft on the BA frequency (see AIP ERSA for the requirements that apply at each location)

items.prompt: Non-controlled aerodromes with an aerodrome — Communications at aerodromes with local flight information services are like those at other non- controlled aerodromes without these services, except that (e)?
items.answer: the service may relay clearances to IFR flights.

items.prompt: Read back requirements — The following parts of a relevant ATC clearance or instruction must always be read back to ATC (a)?
items.answer: ATC route clearances, including any amendments

items.prompt: Amended route or level — The prefixes ‘ AMENDED ’ and ‘ RE CLEARED’ are not used (b)?
items.answer: during normal progressive climb/descent instructions.

However, when asked to ‘ REPORT LAST VACATED LEVEL' this should be the last 100-foo interval the aircraft has passed. This is because ATC may apply a vertical separation based on the reported level.
items.answer: 100 feet
distractors: 50 FT
60 FT

items.prompt: Essential traffic — Essential traffic information may include (a)?
items.answer: direction of flight of aircraft concerned

items.answer: type and wake turbulence category (if relevant) of aircraft concerned

items.answer: estimated time over the reporting point or place where the aircraft's flight paths are expected to cross

items.prompt: Essential traffic — Essential traffic information may include (iv)?
items.answer: for parallel runway operations, the runway being used by the aircraft concerned.

items.prompt: Position reports to ATS — A position report normally comprises. List them.
items.answer: aircraft identification; position; time; level; next position and ETA

items.prompt: Frequency management after take-off — Class D aerodromes 5.8.1.1 After take-off at a Class D aerodrome, pilots should remain on the tower frequency until (a)?
items.answer: if operating in the local circuit – until after the final landing.

items.prompt: Frequency management after take-off — Class C aerodromes 5.8.2.1 If departing from a Class C aerodrome (not remaining in the circuit), pilots should remain on aerodrome frequency until (c)?
items.answer: if operating in the local circuit – until after the final landing.

items.prompt: Training manoeuvres — Pilots may request a variety of training manoeuvres, including (b)?
items.answer: a touch and go – whereby an aircraft lands and takes off without coming to a stop

items.prompt: Training manoeuvres — Pilots may request a variety of training manoeuvres, including (c)?
items.answer: a stop and go – whereby an aircraft lands, stops momentarily on the runway then takes off again

items.prompt: Training manoeuvres — Pilots may request a variety of training manoeuvres, including (d)?
items.answer: for an IFR flight, a precision approach involving a coupled or autoland operation in conditions where ATC is not required to protect the ILS critical or sensitive area

items.prompt: Visual or visual approach — ‘Visual’ 6.6.1.1 The word ‘ visual ’ in radiotelephony means (a)?
items.answer: When used by ATC – an instruction to a pilot to see and avoid obstacles while conducting flight below the relevant lowest safe altitude (LSALT), whether a minimum vectoring altitude

items.prompt: ATS surveillance services – traffic information — Whenever practicable, information regarding traffic on a conflicting path should be given in the following form (a)?
items.answer: relative bearing of the conflicting traffic in terms of the 12-hour clock

items.prompt: ATS surveillance services – traffic information — Whenever practicable, information regarding traffic on a conflicting path should be given in the following form (c)?
items.answer: direction of the flight of the conflicting traffic

items.prompt: ATS surveillance services – traffic information — Whenever practicable, information regarding traffic on a conflicting path should be given in the following form (d)?
items.answer: any other pertinent information such as unknown, slow moving, fast moving, closing, opposite (or same) direction, overtaking, crossing left to right (or right to left), and if known, aircraft type and level, climbing or descending.

items.prompt: Reduced Vertical Separation Minimum (RVSM) — Pilots should report non-approved status during operations in, or vertical transit through, RVSM airspace as follows (a)?
items.answer: at initial call on any channel within RVSM airspace

items.prompt: States of emergency — The states of emergency are classified as follows (a)?
items.answer: Distress: A condition of being threatened by serious and/or imminent danger and of requiring immediate assistance.

items.prompt: States of emergency — The states of emergency are classified as follows (b)?
items.answer: Urgency: A condition concerning the safety of an aircraft or other vehicle, or of some person on board or within sight, but does not require immediate assistance.

items.prompt: Emergency message — what order does the manual give for the content?
items.answer: MAYDAY or PAN PAN three times; name of the station addressed; call sign; type of aircraft; nature of the emergency; intention of the pilot in command; present or last known position, level and heading; pilot qualifications; then any other useful information
distractors: Call sign; MAYDAY three times; nature of the emergency; position; intentions; POB
MAYDAY three times; call sign; position; POB; fuel remaining; intentions
Name of the station addressed; MAYDAY three times; call sign; nature of the emergency; endurance

items.prompt: Emergency message — what does the manual mean by other useful information?
items.answer: For example endurance remaining, POB, aircraft colour or markings, and any survival aids.
distractors: Only the endurance remaining and POB
The aircraft registration and the operator's name
The departure point and destination

items.prompt: Emergency message — are pilot qualifications required in a distress message?
items.answer: No. There is no requirement to include them, but the information may help ATS plan a course of action suited to the pilot's ability.
distractors: Yes, they must always be included
Yes, but only for a student pilot
No, and they should not be transmitted

items.prompt: Emergency message — what pilot qualifications does the manual list?
items.answer: Student pilot; no instrument qualification; private IFR rating; instrument rating
distractors: Student pilot; PPL; CPL; ATPL
No instrument qualification; instrument rating; instructor rating
Student pilot; night VFR; private IFR rating; instrument rating
